delivery.title: Delivery by character
delivery.help: What to haul to each character, and to each of their planets. This is the GROSS consumption for the period — unlike the shopping list, it does not subtract what is already in the launchpad. Every block has its own multibuy to paste into the transfer window. Everything starts collapsed — the summary at the top and each block's header already say what matters without opening anything, and the circle next to the multibuy button marks what you've already delivered this visit.
delivery.empty: Nothing to deliver in this selection.
delivery.footnote: Gross consumption for the period, rounded up per destination — which is why the sum can exceed the shopping list total by a few units: that one subtracts stock and rounds only once.

shopping.stationsNote: Only structures one of your characters can dock at appear here. All of them compete for the hub choice by effective cost (goods + freight).
shopping.noStations: No station found with that name where you can dock.
shopping.noStationsWithMarket: No station with a market for "{query}".
shopping.marketUnconfirmedTooltip: ESI did not answer in time to confirm this station's market. It is shown because we cannot claim it has none — if you add it and there is no book, it drops out of the calculation with a warning.

regionHelp.title: What "Region" means
regionHelp.body: The public market of your home region — the orders across the region's NPC stations. It is the fallback source when an item is not in your structures. Freight is what it costs to haul from those NPC stations to your base. In nullsec it tends to be thin; leave it at 0 if you don't buy there.

jitaHelp.title: What "Jita" means
jitaHelp.body: The public market of The Forge, the game's largest hub. It almost always has the item, and deep. Freight is the ISK/m³ to haul from Jita to your base — courier contract or your own fleet.

shopping.stationNoMarket: No reachable market: this station was left out of the calculation.
shopping.stationsDropped: Left out for lack of market or access: {names}.
shopping.bindingTooltip: Which contract term set this shipment's freight. When the cap (full load) or the floor (collateral / minimum) wins, the total stops being volume × ISK/m³.

contract.noMarginal: Without an ISK/m³ or the full-load m³, freight cannot be attributed per item — hub choice treats this station as zero freight. Provide one of the two.

freightHelp.title: How to work out freight (ISK/m³)
freightHelp.fleetBody: Round-trip fuel cost ÷ m³ you actually carry. E.g. 70.8M ÷ 340,035 m³ = 208 ISK/m³. The trip cost is fixed, so if you don't fill the ship, divide by what you really hauled — flying at 68% costs ~48% more per m³.
freightHelp.courierBody: The ISK/m³ the hauler charges, or reward ÷ m³ of the contract. Many charge “0.5% of collateral or X ISK/m³, whichever is greater”.

shopping.shortTooltip: No hub covers the full quantity: buying it all here will walk the book past what was quoted.

warehouseView.incomplete: One or more Warehouse containers couldn't be read right now — this view may be asking for more than needed (never less).

shopping.stockNote: By default, quantities are the period's gross consumption — they don't discount what's sitting in the colonies' launchpads. PI's ESI only updates a colony when you open the planet in-game, so that stock can be a stale snapshot already used up. What's reliable is the PI Warehouse (real container assets) — the "In stock" column shows that number, and the "Discount stock" button lets you buy only the difference.

shopping.unpriced: {count} item(s) with no book and no reference price — shown without cost, and excluded from the total.
shopping.empty: No bought inputs in this selection.
shopping.footnote: Price walked on the order book for the real quantity, per station. The hub is chosen by effective cost (goods + freight). Click a row for the comparison.

baseHelp.title: What the central base is
baseHelp.body: Where you gather all your PI: the destination of every input you buy and the origin of everything you sell. It is the only hub whose freight is really zero — you are already there. Every other hub is priced by what it costs to haul from it to here.

hubs.baseMissing: No central base set. Pick the structure where you gather your PI — freight is always measured up to it.
hubs.notConfiguredTooltip: No inbound leg on this hub: it enters the hub choice with zero freight. That is not the same as free — pick a method so the number is a real one.
hubs.pickMethod: Pick how the cargo gets from this hub to your base. Until then it counts as zero freight, which is flagged — not the same as free.
hubs.outboundHelp: Only fill this in if you actually deliver your PI here to sell. The sell price still comes from your pricing source (it is not per destination yet), so an outbound leg only ADDS the cost of hauling there.
hubs.optionalHelp: Optional: leave it blank if you do not buy here. It then counts as zero freight, flagged — never silently free.

jf.refuelAtOrigin: Refuel at the origin — the isotope is cheaper there.
jf.refuelAtDestination: Refuel at the base — the isotope is cheaper there.
jf.overridingAdvice: You picked the more expensive side; the numbers below follow your choice.
jf.noIsotopePrice: No sell orders for this isotope at either end: fuel cost unknown. The hub total keeps that uncertainty instead of turning it into zero.
jf.pending: Enter the isotope quantity and the app walks the book to work out ISK/m³.
jf.needQty: Enter the round-trip isotope quantity DOTLAN gave you — the app does not do jump planning.

fieldHelp.perM3: The ISK per m³ the hauler charges on this route. Straight from their rate table.
fieldHelp.minReward: The least the hauler charges per contract, however small the shipment.
fieldHelp.fullLoad: The flat rate the hauler charges for a full freighter load. It is the CEILING: you never pay more than this, however much you send. It is in their rate table.
fieldHelp.fullLoadVolume: The m³ that counts as a "full load" in their table — usually a freighter's capacity (~340,000). Used to turn the ceiling into ISK/m³.
fieldHelp.collateralRate: The fraction of the cargo value the hauler charges (0.005 = 0.5%). Leave empty if the route is "Use Volume" (no collateral term).
fieldHelp.isotopeQty: The isotopes for the WHOLE trip (there and back), as DOTLAN works it out in Jump Planning. One number.
fieldHelp.load: How much your JF really carries per trip — your actual capacity with fit and skills (e.g. ~340,000). The suggested value is the hull's base cargo; replace it with yours.
fieldHelp.outbound: Only fill this in if you sell at this hub (you haul finished PI there). If you sell at your base, leave it closed — the outbound cost is genuinely 0.

rowHelp.revenue: What the exported goods are worth at your sell price, before any tax.

warehouse.pickHelp: Pick the container(s) where you keep your PI. Everything inside them counts as stock — including containers nested inside. A container is anything of yours that holds other items, so a parked freighter works too.

warehouse.autonomyHelp: Stock divided by what the whole PORTFOLIO consumes per hour. It answers "when do I need to buy", not "will colony X stall" — the material still has to be hauled to specific colonies, and the per-colony alarm lives in the planet alerts.

config.exportTaxHint: Global default for standalone colonies (0–100%). Networks can override per network.
config.importTaxHint: POCO tax on bought inputs (0–100%). Defaults to the export tax.
config.visitCadenceHint: How often you restock a planet (hours). Buffers that won't last until your next visit trigger the alert. Default = 24h.
config.homeRegionHint: The region you trade in — sets local market pricing. Default = Jita.
config.pricingHelp:
How Jita prices are applied:

• Import buy / export sell (default): optimistic — buy inputs at the best buy order, sell output at the best sell order (patient limit orders). Highest ISK/h.
• Mid price: midpoint of buy and sell.
• Pessimistic: buy at the sell order (walking the asks), sell at the buy order — what you get dumping to the market instantly. Lowest ISK/h.
• Realistic: buy inputs via multibuy (walking the asks, like pessimistic), but sell outputs at your configured sell source (e.g. Jita split). Matches an operation that multibuys inputs and sells outputs via contract, not an instant dump.

The default assumes patient trading on both sides, so real profit is usually lower.

rattingHelp.title: Ratting Configuration Guide
rattingHelp.description: Learn how to configure and maximize your automatic profit tracking with Ratting.
rattingHelp.characterPreparationText: For automatic tracking to work, your characters must be linked to EasyEve with the correct permissions.
rattingHelp.walletScopeText: Wallet Scope: It is essential that the character has the Wallet Journal read scope active. Without this, EasyEve cannot see Bounties and ESS payments.
rattingHelp.walletScopeHelp: It is essential that the character has the Wallet Journal read scope active. Without this, EasyEve cannot see Bounties and ESS payments.
rattingHelp.activeTokensHelp: Check on the characters screen if the token status is green. Expired tokens prevent synchronization.
rattingHelp.stepAText: Click on "Start New Activity" and select the Ratting icon (red crosshair).
rattingHelp.stepBText: Select the characters that will participate in the fleet and the local NPC Faction.
rattingHelp.note: The system uses Faction and Site Name to suggest the best bonuses and calculate estimates.
rattingHelp.iskSyncText: EasyEve doesn't "read your screen", it queries the CCP server for new wallet journal entries.
rattingHelp.bountyTicksHelp: Synchronized every 20 minutes (standard game time). Use the "Sync ESI" button to update.
rattingHelp.bountyTicksText: Bounty Ticks: Synchronized every 20 minutes (standard game time). Use the "Sync ESI" button to update.
rattingHelp.essPayoutsHelp: Appear in the wallet about 3 hours after the activity. If you close the activity, EasyEve will continue monitoring for 4 more hours.
rattingHelp.essPayoutsText: ESS Payouts: Appear in the wallet about 3 hours after the activity. If you close the activity, EasyEve will continue monitoring for 4 more hours.
rattingHelp.importantText: CCP ESI may have a cache delay of up to 5 minutes. If you just received the tick in-game, wait a few moments before syncing.
rattingHelp.expertTip1: Prioritize Havens (Rock) and Sanctums for best ISK/Hour in Nullsec.
rattingHelp.expertTip2: Always click "Sync ESI" before finishing the activity to ensure the last tick was captured.
rattingHelp.expertTip3: ISK/hr calculation considers net profit accumulated divided by total operation time.

helpModal.subtitle: Follow these steps to configure and launch your fleet operation

helpModal.tip: Need more help? Click the ? button next to each configuration option for detailed explanations specific to that activity type.

tour.stepFleetDescription: Select the characters joining this operation and assign fits when needed.

ratting.title: Ratting Guide
ratting.subtitle: Track your ratting income and anomalies
ratting.whatIsIt: Ratting tracks your NPC combat income from anomaly running. EasyEve syncs with CCP ESI to capture bounty ticks and ESS payouts automatically.
ratting.step1: Select your Security Level (Highsec, Lowsec, Nullsec, Wormhole)
ratting.step2: Choose your Hostile Faction based on the space you're ratting in
ratting.step3: Select the specific Anomaly from the detected list
ratting.step4: Optionally enable Auto Loot Tracking to track MTU/container loot
ratting.importantNote: Bounty ticks sync every 20 minutes. Click "Sync ESI" before ending the activity to capture the last tick.

mining.title: Mining Guide
mining.subtitle: Track your mining yield and ore values
mining.whatIsIt: Mining tracks your ore/ice/gas extraction and calculates market values in real-time based on current prices.
mining.step1: Select your Security Level (Highsec, Lowsec, Nullsec, Wormhole)
mining.step2: Choose Mining Category: Ore, Ice, Gas, or Moon
mining.step3: View the Valuable Ores preview to see expected yields
mining.importantNote: Prices update automatically. You can configure which ores to track in your profile settings.

abyssal.title: Abyssal Guide
abyssal.subtitle: Track your abyssal filament runs
abyssal.whatIsIt: Abyssal tracking calculates your net profit by comparing cargo before and after each run. Enter your initial cargo state to start.
abyssal.step1: Before running abyssal, open your cargo and copy all item names/quantities
abyssal.step2: Paste the cargo contents into the "Initial Cargo State" field
abyssal.step3: After completing the run, enter new cargo to calculate profit
abyssal.importantNote: The more detailed your cargo entry (with quantities), the more accurate your profit calculation will be.

exploration.title: Exploration Guide
exploration.subtitle: Track your relic and data sites
exploration.whatIsIt: Exploration tracks loot from relic and data sites. Enter your initial cargo to calculate what you found during exploration.
exploration.step1: Before scanning sites, copy your current cargo contents
exploration.step2: Paste into the "Initial Cargo State" field
exploration.step3: After exploring, add your collected loot to track total value
exploration.importantNote: You can add exploration loot manually during the activity. The system will calculate the delta from your initial state.

salvaging.title: Salvaging Guide
salvaging.subtitle: Track loot from wreck salvaging
salvaging.whatIsIt: Salvaging tracks loot gained while salvaging wrecks. Paste your cargo before and after each run; the saved after-cargo becomes the baseline for the next batch.
salvaging.step1: Select the NPC faction whose wrecks you are salvaging (Angel, Guristas, Blood Raider, etc.)
salvaging.step2: After salvaging, paste your full cargo hold in the register loot dialog
salvaging.step3: Repeat as you salvage more wrecks — each after-cargo chains as the next before-cargo
salvaging.importantNote: lastCargoState is updated after every successful registration, same as Exploration and Abyssal.

pvp.title: PVP Guide
pvp.subtitle: Track your PVP activities
pvp.whatIsIt: PVP tracking helps you record combat statistics and ship losses. More features coming soon.
pvp.step1: Select PVP as your activity type and add participating characters
pvp.step2: Manually log combat events and ship losses during the activity
pvp.step3: End the activity to view your combat summary

crab.title: CRAB Guide
crab.subtitle: Track your pirate faction sites
crab.whatIsIt: CRAB (Combat Anomaly Burn) tracks Pirate Faction sites similar to ratting. More features coming soon.
crab.step1: Select CRAB as your activity type
crab.step2: Configure space type and faction settings
crab.step3: Track your site completion times and rewards

escalations.title: Escalations Guide
escalations.subtitle: Track DED/escalated sites
escalations.whatIsIt: Escalations track DED-rated sites and their valuable loot, including purchases, sales, and automatic bounty/ESS sync. Start tracking your DED site profits now!
escalations.step1: Select Escalations as your activity type
escalations.step2: Track completed sites and their loot values
escalations.step3: View your escalation success rate and ISK/hour
